# naming.procedure.coroutine-compilation-and-runtime-routing

Kind: `native-observation`

## Problem statement

Tailcall and coroutine heads can use a compiler placeholder or a runtime procedure namespace, and operand-time rename can change the target. A printed command name cannot decide either compilation or frame routing.

## Question

What original disassembly and runtime namespace/frame/completion behavior do the coroutine and tailcall controls retain?

## Conclusion

Compilation tables and thirteen runtime programs remain independent. The captured releases differ in compiler availability and placeholder replacement; namespace/caller routing, expansion, rename, deletion and illegal yield retain their own outcomes. Missing Jim coroutine commands are actual rejected doors, not an entered coroutine.

## Scope

Only the original retained programs, capture windows and provider labels in the attached artifacts are covered. Version labels are original receipt metadata, not a fresh patchlevel query. Missing command/API doors and aborted processes stay distinct from successful guest completion. Source files/probes explain the observer protocol; no pinned engine implementation excerpt or executed Rust assertion is claimed. Different attempts and sources are retained separately, never treated as byte-identical duplicates.
